name: quake2
title: QUAKE II 3.19 (ref_soft, C_ONLY)
_doc: Twice the program Quake 1 is, and the point of picking it: it needs no environment PRISM does not already have, so it turns 'does this scale?' from a question into a measurement.
_defines: C_ONLY is id's OWN switch, and a cleaner one than Quake 1's: q_shared.h:42 reads `#if (defined _M_IX86 || defined __i386__) && !defined C_ONLY`, so defining it selects the portable C body of every routine that has an assembly twin -- r_draw.c/r_drawa.asm, r_edge.c/r_edgea.asm, r_scan.c/r_scana.asm, r_polyse.c/r_polysa.asm. A build option, not a source edit.
_units: The object lists of linux/Makefile.i386, with the null platform in place of the Linux one. Each shared object of a real build is linked in ONCE here, so q_shared.c and glob.c -- which the makefile compiles separately into quake2 and into ref_soft.so -- appear a single time.
_files: What the INSTALLATION provides, as against what the player provides. vid_so.c reads one line from /etc/quake2.conf and treats it as the directory holding the ref libraries; on a real Linux box the package put it there. A dot means the current directory, which is where dlopen looks anyway -- it matches on the last component. This is not game data and does not belong in the data directory, and it is not a source change: it is the file the program has always read.
_input: linux/vid_so.c, NOT null/vid_null.c + null/in_null.c. The direct-link glue got the renderer running and cost the KEYBOARD: null/in_null.c is empty stubs, and it is vid_so.c that dlsyms KBD_Init/KBD_Update/KBD_Close and the six RW_IN_* out of the refresh and assigns KBD_Update_fp. Without it Sys_SendKeyEvents (linux/sys_linux.c:256) finds a null pointer every frame, so the game renders, runs its server and plays its demo while being completely deaf -- measured: KBD_Update called 0 times in 60 frames. vid_so.c dlopens `ref_soft.so` (the name sprintf'd at vid_so.c:357 from the vid_ref cvar), which is why the module needs a soname.
_null: null/ is not a stub set here, it is the DIRECT LINK: null/vid_null.c is titled 'DIRECT LINK GLUE' and calls GetRefAPI in-process, where linux/vid_so.c and win32/vid_dll.c dlopen ref_soft.so for it. So this build needs no dlopen. What null/ does NOT give is the game: null/sys_null.c:37 has Sys_GetGameAPI return NULL, so game/ compiles but the server cannot reach it.
_inline: What every real platform's in_*.c defines and id's own null platform does not -- linux/in_linux.c:6 and win32/in_win.c:55 both have exactly this line. cvar_t is left incomplete on purpose: only the pointer is needed here. It stays NULL, because a platform's IN_Init is what registers it and null/in_null.c's is empty -- so opening the Options menu would dereference NULL, in id's own null build just as much as in this one. Faithful, and stated rather than papered over.
_modules: Quake II is THREE shared objects in a real build and stays three here, each with its own external namespace -- which is the only way qcommon/common.c:101, game/g_main.c:154 and ref_soft/r_main.c:1410 can each keep their own Com_Printf, routed through their own import struct. A module sees its own symbols and the main one's, which is ELF's rule for a shared object against the executable's globals; everything else reaches it through the struct of function pointers the program hands it. What travels the other way is the module's EXPORTS, read from the program's own .def file -- `EXPORTS GetRefAPI` and `EXPORTS GetGameAPI`, one symbol each.

ref_soft._rw: linux/rw_x11.c is REF_SOFT_OBJS too -- the makefile builds ref_softx.so from the same renderer plus this one file. It is what ALLOCATES the surface: null/swimp_null.c is empty bodies and its SWimp_SetMode returns nothing, so vid.buffer stayed 0. rw_x11.c does it with XCreateImage, over the Xlib PRISM already had for Doom.

game._doc: linux/Makefile.i386's GAME_OBJS. q_shared.c and m_flash.c are NOT repeated here even though the real build compiles them into the game too: a module already sees the main one's symbols, which is where those live.
game._newer: g_chase.c is not in GAME_OBJS either, and g_cmds.c and p_client.c call four of its functions. Same finding as cl_newfx.c: linux/Makefile.i386 is older than the source beside it.

_net: null/ has no network stub -- Quake 1 shipped net_none.c and Quake II did not -- and the engine's own loopback, which is what single player runs on, lives INSIDE the platform file (NET_GetLoopPacket in linux/net_udp.c). So the faithful move is the program's own file with the OS calls stubbed, not a hand-written null layer: the loopback path touches no socket at all.
_data: Its own demo, which id distributed freely: q2-314-demo-x86.exe, 39,015,499 bytes, sha1 5b4dedc59ceee306956a3e48a8bdf6dd33bc91ed, from the GWDG mirror of ftp.idsoftware.com/idstuff/quake2/. It is a plain zip; Install/Data/baseq2/ is the tree, and baseq2/pak0.pak is 49,951,322 bytes holding 1106 files. It lives OUTSIDE the repository, in a directory the user names, like every other target's data.
_platform: linux/sys_linux.c rather than null/sys_null.c, and the reason is the game. The refresh had direct-link glue (null/vid_null.c calls GetRefAPI in process); the game has none anywhere in the tree, and null/sys_null.c:37 simply returns NULL for it. linux/sys_linux.c:196 is the only Sys_GetGameAPI that does the real thing -- dlopen(gamei386.so), dlsym(GetGameAPI) -- so the faithful path is the program's own file over a dlopen that resolves against PRISM's symbol table.
_state: Renders. 109 units, 88,161 lines, 2142 functions, nothing unemitted; 320x240, 177 distinct colours, ~144 frames/s on the demo. Three modules bridged where the program bridges them: the refresh through GetRefAPI (null/vid_null.c's direct-link glue), the game through dlopen/dlsym over PRISM's symbol table. linux/rw_x11.c is what gives ref_soft a surface -- null/swimp_null.c's SWimp_SetMode returns nothing at all, so vid.buffer stayed 0.
_newfx: client/cl_newfx.c is NOT in linux/Makefile.i386 -- that makefile predates it -- but cl_tent.c and cl_ents.c call 23 of its functions. The undefined-symbol report is what found it; before that the build claimed to be complete and the effects would have thrown when fired.

variants._doc: The base target IS the Linux client. A variant is another of the platform layers id shipped -- and the one thing that mattered when this was written is that Solaris's is not a client at all.

solaris.title: QUAKE II q2ded (Solaris)
solaris._doc: EVERY UNIT is from solaris/Makefile.Solaris, whose target is `q2ded` -- id's Solaris port is a DEDICATED SERVER and nothing else. cl_null.c and cd_null.c are in its object list, there is no rw_* or vid_* anywhere in solaris/, and the makefile links no renderer. So this has no picture by construction: it is the server half of Quake II, which is also the half no other target here exercises on its own.

game._doc: linux/Makefile.i386's GAME_OBJS. q_shared.c and m_flash.c are NOT repeated here even though the real build compiles them into the game too: a module already sees the main one's symbols, which is where those live.
game._newer: g_chase.c is not in GAME_OBJS either, and g_cmds.c and p_client.c call four of its functions. Same finding as cl_newfx.c: linux/Makefile.i386 is older than the source beside it.

solaris._modules: Only the game. sv_game.c still dlopens gamei386.so -- solaris/g_so.c is that object's own build -- and there is no refresh to load.

win32.title: QUAKE II 3.19 (Win32, ref_soft, C_ONLY)
win32._doc: id's Win32 client, and the fifth platform layer over this engine. THE UNIT LIST IS NOT TRANSCRIBED FROM quake2.mak, on purpose: that makefile is OLDER THAN THE SOURCE BESIDE IT -- seven of its forty-one objects (cl_demo, sbar2, scr_cin, screen, sv_move, sv_phys, view) name files 3.19 no longer has, and one of ref_soft's (r_inter) likewise. It is the same staleness P7.7 found in linux/Makefile.i386, so the engine list is the one the Linux target already proves and only the FIVE platform files are swapped: sys_linux/q_shlinux/vid_so/net_udp/glob become sys_win/q_shwin/vid_dll/net_wins -- and glob.c has no twin because q_shwin.c implements Sys_FindFirst itself. Sound and CD stay on the tree's own null drivers, the same build selection the Linux variant makes. ONE BUILD SELECTION WAS WRONG AND THE LINKER SAID SO: this variant first took the tree's own null sound and CD drivers, carried over from the Linux one. But S_Activate is defined ONLY in win32/snd_win.c and win32/vid_dll.c calls it on every window activation -- on Linux vid_so.c does not. So the null drivers are not a selection id's Win32 tree offers, and this build takes snd_win.c and cd_win.c as it shipped. That costs nothing, because src/env/win32.c was designed for exactly this: LoadLibrary returns NULL so the DirectSound path stands down, waveOutOpen fails so the fallback gives up, and mciSendCommand fails so CDAudio reports no drive.

ref_soft._rw: quake2.mak builds ref_soft.dll from the renderer plus rw_imp, rw_dib and rw_ddraw: rw_imp.c is the platform half, rw_dib.c the GDI surface and rw_ddraw.c the DirectDraw one. The DIB path is the one PRISM already serves for WinQuake and PuTTY.

game._doc: linux/Makefile.i386's GAME_OBJS. q_shared.c and m_flash.c are NOT repeated here even though the real build compiles them into the game too: a module already sees the main one's symbols, which is where those live.
game._newer: g_chase.c is not in GAME_OBJS either, and g_cmds.c and p_client.c call four of its functions. Same finding as cl_newfx.c: linux/Makefile.i386 is older than the source beside it.

win32._defines: The platform macros MSVC defines for a Win32 build, the same pair targets/quake.json's win variant carries. Not a convenience: win32/rw_dib.c opens with #ifndef _WIN32 and its own #error, so the file refuses to compile without them -- the program stating its own platform requirement, which is configuration rather than modification. C_ONLY comes from the base target and selects the renderer's C paths over its assembly, the same choice as Quake's id386=0. NDEBUG, _M_IX86 and CPUSTRING come from the same place: they are what the Win32 project file passes, and the SOURCE reads them. sys_win.c picks its debugdir inside #ifdef branches on _M_IX86 and NDEBUG -- with neither defined no branch declares it at all -- and common.c prints CPUSTRING in its version banner. Configuration the build states, not a patch.
win32._generated: The Win32 shim is COMPILED, not registered as an environment module: win32-app.c is its non-graphical half (last error, code pages, module handles) and win32.c is the window and its message queue, both in C because their contracts are structs the program reads and writes. Same pair targets/quake.json's win variant pulls in -- minus mgl.c, which is WinQuake's renderer boundary and not Quake II's: this one draws through GDI, from win32/rw_dib.c. win32-net.c is the third: the wsock ENV supplies primitives (prism_net_open, prism_net_send and the rest) and this file is Winsock itself written over them, which is why env alone left WSAStartup and closesocket undefined -- and why win32.c called a prism_net_pump nobody defined. PuTTY reaches it the same way.
win32._args: demo1 is the map the DATA here has, and it is what web/programs/quake2.json already uses for the Linux client. This variant said base1 for a while, copied from the solaris one -- which is a DEDICATED SERVER and so never had to draw what it loaded. vid_fullscreen 0 is the real branch selector: rw_imp.c takes DIB_Init when windowed and DDRAW_Init when not, and DirectDraw is declared here and refused.
win32._modules: BOTH modules, because a variant's block REPLACES the base's rather than extending it -- declaring only ref_soft dropped `game`, LoadLibrary found no gamex86.dll and Quake II said so: 'failed to load game DLL'. The soname is the Win32 one from sys_win.c:479; the same module is gamei386.so on Linux and the .def file it exports from is the same either way.

gl.title: QUAKE II 3.19 (Linux, ref_gl on fxMesa, C_ONLY)
gl._doc: The client the base target is, with the renderer linux/Makefile.i386 builds as ref_gl.so: REF_GL_OBJS -- the nine ref_gl/*.c, linux/qgl_linux.c, linux/gl_fxmesa.c (Mesa's full-screen 3Dfx context; that build has no GLX) and linux/rw_in_svgalib.c for keys and the mouse. q_shared.c, q_shlinux.c and glob.c are in REF_GL_OBJS too but, as for ref_soft, a module sees the main one's copies. OpenGL is src/env/gl.js, fxMesa src/env/fxmesa.js, svgalib src/env/svgalib.js. vid_so.c loads ref_<vid_ref>.so, so +set vid_ref gl selects it.

files../ref_gl.so: (linked into this program; the file is what the package installs, and vid_so.c stat()s it and wants it owned by root)

gl._files: The installation, as for the base target: /etc/quake2.conf names the ref directory, and ref_gl.so is there because the package put it there. vid_so.c stat()s every ref but softx and refuses one not owned by root -- svgalib needs root -- so the file must exist; PRISM's only user is root.
gl._fps: The page paces this variant at 60 frames a second. The descriptor's 30 was set for the software renderer; ref_gl on WebGL2 draws demo1 at 115-120 unpaced (measured in the page with speed unlimited), and Quake II's own cl_maxfps defaults to 90.

win32gl.title: QUAKE II 3.19 (Win32, ref_gl on opengl32, C_ONLY)
win32gl._doc: id's Win32 client with the GL renderer: the win32 variant's client and game, and ref_gl.dll -- quake2.mak's ref_gl project, the nine renderer files plus win32/glw_imp.c (the window and its WGL context) and win32/qgl_win.c (LoadLibrary("opengl32") and a GetProcAddress for every gl and wgl entry point). opengl32.dll is src/env/opengl32.c over src/env/gl.js, the layer the Linux GL build already draws on.
